content.text:
---
name: pi-dish-sessions
description: Spawn, message, and read ordinary peer Pi sessions through the pi-dish server, and search every past session transcript — locally or across the whole host fleet. Use when work should run in a separate durable Pi process, when another session needs a prompt, steer, follow-up, interrupt, resume, or graceful termination, when a prompt carries a session ref or a `#ref` mention (like "#tycho/8f3ab2c1") or a `<session-refs>` block and you need to read or talk to that session, or when prior sessions may already hold the answer (how something was fixed or built before, where a file was touched, what a past investigation concluded).
---

# Pi-dish peer sessions

Use the bundled CLI. It talks only to pi-dish's semantic HTTP routes; it
never writes Pi JSONL or signals processes itself.

```bash
CLI=~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-dish-sessions/scripts/pi-dish-sessions.js
node "$CLI" list --active
```

`PI_DISH_URL` is inherited by sessions spawned through pi-dish and otherwise
defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:3333`; set `PI_DISH_TOKEN` when the server
requires a bearer. The CLI identifies the current session automatically; use
`--session <id>` only if it reports ambiguity. `--json` everywhere for
machine-readable output.

## Session refs

Anywhere a command takes a session id, it takes a **ref**: a full id, its
uuid tail, a unique ≥4-char prefix of either (`01a070d2`), or a
host-qualified form (`tycho/01a070d2` — no `--host` needed). `list`,
`search` and `resolve` print the shortest ref for each session in their
first column; pass that along. Never retype an encoded `~sk1_…` route id —
it is ~100 base64 characters and a one-character slip still decodes, so the
server can only say `Session not found`. Users copy refs from the pi-dish
UI; treat a pasted short id as a ref, and `resolve <ref>` to see what it
points at.

A prompt written in the pi-dish composer can carry `#ref` mentions, and the
server appends a `<session-refs>` block listing each one with its name, host
and cwd. Those are live handles, not citations: `read` the session before
reasoning about what it did, and `send`/`steer`/`follow-up` to talk to it.

## Hot path

```bash
node "$CLI" search "jsonl torn tail recovery" --limit 5   # find prior work
node "$CLI" search "index compaction" --all-hosts          # whole fleet
node "$CLI" read tycho/8f3ab2c1                            # transcript as markdown
node "$CLI" send <ref> "Run the tests"                     # prompt (queues mid-turn)
node "$CLI" steer <ref> "Check the nested case first"      # redirect current turn
node "$CLI" follow-up <ref> "Then summarize here"          # queue for after the turn
node "$CLI" spawn --cwd "$PWD" --name "investigation" \
  --prompt "Investigate the cache issue and report" --json # durable peer process
node "$CLI" resume <ref>                                   # revive an inactive session
```

A spawned peer runs the same harness as the session spawning it (Pi from Pi,
OMP from OMP), so it has the same tools and skills you do. Pass
`--harness pi|omp|prime` to cross over deliberately; the spawn result names
the harness it launched.

Search treats the session corpus as long-term memory: before re-deriving a
fix, config, or investigation, check whether a prior session already did it.
If a first query misses, reformulate with terms you'd expect *in the
transcript* — an error string, a file path, a command line. Search finds the
session; `read` reads it.

Also available: `show` (raw JSON window), `related`, `interrupt`, `close`
(graceful, no force-kill), `hosts` (the fleet; `--host <name>` puts any
command on that host), `attach` (join a live session's tmux pane from this
terminal — local only), `resolve`, `session`.

## Going deeper

- `node "$CLI" --help` and `help <command>` — full flags and examples.
- `node "$CLI" docs` — server-versioned topics (`refs`, `search` grammar,
  `fleet` semantics, `sessions` control details). In a mixed-version fleet
  the server's own docs beat this file; `docs --host <name>` reads a peer's.

3:Status: **M0, M1 and M5 accepted; M2, M3, M4 and M6 remain in progress**.

6:contract, shared-helper and lifecycle stages. Their implementation records remain
7:historical evidence; this document does not reopen those stages by default.
8:
9:## Mission and sequencing
10:
11:Finish the implementations and compiler boundaries that still need migration,
12:then perform explicit simplifying refactors on the checked application. Moving a
13:function, introducing a type, shortening `server.js`, or replacing JavaScript with
14:TypeScript is not by itself a simplification result.
15:
16:The remaining work has three separately accepted phases:
17:
18:1. **Migration:** actual product implementations and their consumers become
19:   checked, with preserved behavior and supported runtime entrypoints.
20:2. **Simplification:** remove identified competing responsibilities, unnecessary
21:   indirection and cross-domain coupling in the now-checked application, including
22:   the already-TypeScript browser. This is committed scope, not optional cleanup.
23:3. **Repository closure:** finish tests/tooling, make coverage and exceptions
24:   enforceable, and prove delivery/build consistency across the supported surfaces.
25:
26:Migration packages may remove adapters made obsolete by their own cutover, but
27:must not silently redesign operation policy or user workflows. The larger
28:simplifying refactors have their own contracts, deletion ledgers and behavior
29:checks. Test/tooling source conversion does not block the product refactor phase;
30:it does block claiming the repository migration is finished.
31:
32:## Current position and measurement
33:
34:The baseline has 155 authored product TypeScript files (1,632,779 bytes) and 30
35:product JavaScript files (549,637 bytes). Browser source accounts for 106 of those
36:TS files; core for 42; harness extensions for seven. Extensions are not included
37:in the main strict compiler programs merely because their filenames end in `.ts`.
38:The backend subset (`src/core/`, authored `lib/`, `server.js`) is 49.5% TS by
39:source bytes. Product source is 74.8% TS by bytes; neither is an effort estimate.
40:
41:These figures count tracked JS/TS product sources, excluding generated outputs,
42:vendor files, historical documentation, tests and development tooling. The
43:GitHub language bar counts generated JavaScript and substantial JS test/tooling
44:source; it is not a migration acceptance gate. Keep four separate measures:
45:authored implementation inventory; compiler-program coverage; removed competing
46:owners/paths; and verified delivery. Do not claim a performance or complexity
47:improvement from source size alone.
48:
49:The baseline passed strict/drift checks, 996 backend tests, 286 browser cases,
50:eight isolated UI scenarios, full desktop/mobile smoke, and real OMP/Prime
51:canaries. [All five CI jobs passed on the baseline commit](https://github.com/MrPink604/pi-dish/actions/runs/34963611465).
52:Those counts describe the starting point, not a required permanent test count or
53:verification of the future work below.
54:
55:## Invariants and scope limits
56:
57:- Preserve native/route/host identity distinctions and captured asynchronous
58:  ownership. A cache, catalog row, relationship hint, type brand or read snapshot
59:  never becomes permission to control a process.
60:- Preserve capability gates, launch-token/process-birth/registry proofs and final
61:  action-time revalidation. Do not flatten distinct lifecycle conflicts,
62:  quarantines or uncertain outcomes into a generic operation lock.
63:- Preserve API, store, JSONL and harness wire compatibility, including absent,
64:  null, malformed, fallback and partial-result behavior. First-party consumed
65:  fields are closed contracts; opaque external payloads remain unknown until
66:  consumed. No universal schema for every harness/tool/extension event.
67:- Preserve bounded/incremental reads, cache invalidation, retained transcript DOM,
68:  streaming coalescing and pagination. Record meaningful I/O/allocation effects
69:  before claiming a reduction; do not replace bounded paths with whole-corpus
70:  normalization.
71:- Keep local browser assets, existing deployment entrypoints and native loader
72:  behavior. A new compiler target is not permission to adopt ESM, add a production
73:  TS loader, change the Node minimum, or redesign packaging silently.
74:- Reuse existing state writers, domain owners and `dish-store`. No universal
75:  repository/service framework, catch-all capability bag, global event bus or
76:  framework adoption. No `any`/`@ts-nocheck`/unchecked handwritten declaration
77:  workaround to make implementation coverage appear complete.
78:- Named interfaces belong to the owner of a boundary. Newly introduced or
79:  renegotiated public ports must not derive from a concrete factory's `ReturnType`.
80:  R9 removes the specified existing hub-controller coupling; untouched legacy
81:  factory-derived ports are not silently claimed eliminated. No compatibility
82:  alias chains or type-only facade asserting an unchecked implementation is safe.
83:- Preserve unrelated local work and isolate tests from live sessions, credentials,
84:  user HOME, sockets and tmux servers.
85:
86:## Package and review contract
87:
88:Every package below is an implementation/review unit, not a promised single
89:commit. Before edits, its owner freezes the consumed-field/behavior matrix,
90:source and caller inventory, target owner, dependency edges and relevant smoke
91:fixtures. Contract changes return to the integration owner before concurrent
92:workers proceed. Producers and consumers that cannot coexist safely ship together.
93:
94:Each completion record must contain:
95:
96:1. Actual source and consumer cutover, compiler program and runtime output paths.
97:2. Removed implementation/adapters/state owners; distinguish moves from deletions.
98:3. Preserved edge cases and any separately approved policy change.
99:4. Focused behavior evidence plus applicable integration/runtime gates.
100:5. Explicit remaining unchecked or opaque boundaries, with no hidden new exception.
101:
102:For simplification packages, also compare the contributor path for one concrete
103:change before and after: who owns the state/transition, which independently
104:maintained interpretations disappeared, and whether a new facade merely hid the
105:same coupling. File/line-count reductions are supporting inventory, not acceptance.
106:
107:The integration lead maintains the implementation ledger in this document under
108:one `Implementation record — <package ID>` subsection per completed M/R/C package
109:(including separately landed subpackages). Each record names source commit(s),
110:owner, actual checks/runtime versions/skips, removed owners/paths, retained
111:boundaries and exact CI/review links. The package author supplies the evidence;
112:an independent reviewer checks the ledger against code and behavior, and the
113:integration lead records acceptance and updates BACKLOG. If a package needs its
114:own substantial design record, link it from that subsection rather than creating
115:an untracked parallel clearance list. Planning critique alone never accepts a
116:future implementation package.
117:
118:## Complete remaining ownership inventory
119:
120:The following assignment covers all 30 authored product JS files at the baseline.
121:Generated `lib` files are excluded. Server ranges below identify the baseline
122:seams; they are not permanent line-number contracts.
123:
124:| Package | Authored implementations and associated consumers |
125:| --- | --- |
126:| M1 Read/SDK/projections | `lib/session-files.js`, `pi-sdk.js`, `omp-export.js`, `session-refs.js`, `harness-pricing.js`, `skill-mining.js`; typed index/metadata consumers and session read/export/tree/usage response production |
127:| M2 Automation | `lib/cron.js`, `routines.js`, `routine-runner.js`, `session-provenance.js`; routine HTTP/prompt/ledger composition and catalog provenance |
128:| M3 Publication/files | `lib/pages.js`, `shares.js`, `comments.js`, `fleet-artifacts.js`, `file-search.js`, `file-mention.js`, `file-page.js`, `git-diff.js`; publication/comment/file/diff routes |
129:| M4 Feature projections/integrations | `lib/skills.js`, `harness-agents.js`, `stt.js`; server usage aggregation, skill coverage/refinement and harness settings/command/model adapters |
130:| M5 Transport/terminal | `lib/remote-hosts.js`, `terminal.js`; HTTP access/tickets/CORS, fleet HTTP/public/WS relay and PTY attachment |
131:| M6 Runtime edges | `skills/lib/pi-dish-client.js`, the sessions/comments/pages skill CLIs, `electron/main.js`, `extensions/pi-dish-share-omp.mjs`; all seven existing extension TS implementations also enter strict checking |
132:| M7 Server completion | Remaining `server.js` implementation, including route mounting, session controls, SSE projection/replay, configuration/utilities and startup/shutdown |
133:
134:M1 owns the shared Pi SDK, pricing and skill-mining implementation edits; M4 owns
135:their feature aggregation/HTTP consumers. M2 owns provenance. M3 owns artifact

production-composition, Bounce and desktop/mobile cases remain intact.

### R9 — One ordered selection-retirement sequence and narrow ports

**After:** R8. Keep `session-view` authoritative. Factor shared retirement phases
currently repeated by provisional and real selection; activation/chrome paths
remain distinct. Replace whole-controller factory-return inputs in session view
and message stream with owner-defined consumed-method interfaces.

**Proof:** one reviewed ordering for selection advancement, mark clearing, draft/
DOM stashing, stream/request retirement and activity reset. Unknown targets still
leave the current view intact. No universal cancellation generation or merger of
stream/transcript owners. Type negatives reject unrelated controller operations;
selection/spawn/composer/terminal/transcript/late-ticket cases prove behavior.

### R10 — Endpoint-explicit browser mutations

**After:** M gate; can run alongside R8 with a separate file owner.

Replace `session-controls`' per-mutation `createSessionApi` construction and
ignored-host closure with explicit API mutation operations accepting the captured
endpoint and session identity. Selection ownership remains in controls; transport
does not need a selection generation just to address a request.

**Proof:** no per-mutation factory allocation or host-argument substitution;
model/thinking/rename callers, exports and type fixtures migrate together.
Preserve latest-operation ordering, endpoint-base checks, refreshed credentials
and patching the original session after selection changes. Existing API/control/
delayed-mutation/endpoint-change cases plus real multi-host UI smoke are gates.

### R11 — One canonical reference algorithm across app and skill client

**After:** M6b. Bundle existing portable `src/core/helper-refs.ts` behavior into
the generated skill client; remove its copies of alias generation, staged
resolution and stable/short references. Keep the installed client dependency-free.

**Proof:** one authored algorithm; existing semantic precedence/ambiguity/
host-qualified exact-only cases pass through real CLI and browser/server paths.
Preserve the CLI's differing missing-native-ID parsing policy explicitly; do not
blindly replace its decoder with stricter canonical decoding. Remove copy-parity
tests that become wiring assertions, retaining consumer behavior coverage.

### R12 — Remove the handwritten vendor module loader

**After:** the vendor-tool source/runner portion of C1 is ready (it may land
earlier than the remainder of C1). Use existing pinned esbuild for the local
highlight bundle instead of `build-vendor`'s dependency collector and generated
`__mods`/`__cache`/`__req` implementation.

**Proof:** manual loader/resolver/cache wrappers deleted; `window.hljs`, common
languages, licenses and offline highlighting preserved. CSS/fonts and unrelated
vendor delivery stay unchanged. Rebuild vendor outputs only for this package;
exercise actual offline code rendering. No new bundler abstraction.

### Deliberate limits on refactoring

The scoping workers identified possible stale-stat/short-read index publication
risks, but did not reproduce corruption. M1's malformed/append/truncate matrix
must exercise the consumed-byte/stamp invariant. A demonstrated violation becomes
a focused regression/fix; a speculative transactional index/cache rewrite is not
part of the mandatory refactor list. No stronger atomicity claim is made here.

Also excluded: unifying differing header/cwd/recovery parsers; a generic terminal
routine “finish and close”; merging pricing persistence with generic store writes
despite permission/newline differences; merging interactive/pricing command
runners; broad host-catalog extraction from new-session forms; framework adoption.
Future ideas require their own problem/evidence, not expansion of this finish line.

## Phase C — Repository closure

### C1 — Checked tests, fixtures, development tools and configurations

**Depends on:** stable product contracts. Its runner/vendor-tool prerequisite may
start alongside late M/R work; test-family cutovers wait for the contract they use.

Convert the authored scripts (nine at baseline, plus M0's source-policy gate and
later additions), Node tests, Playwright tests, UI scenarios and support
implementations in bounded families. Explicitly allocate
`eslint.config.js` and `playwright.config.js`: keep compatible loader entrypoints
as named strict-`checkJs` configurations unless their hosts support a direct TS
cutover without a new runtime loader. Their bodies are checked, not deferred to
the final audit. Keep Node and browser-evaluation compiler environments separate.
Preserve intentional malformed inputs as unknown or explicit negative cases
rather than weakening product types.

Freeze the execution mapping before renaming: `run-tests.js` discovers only
`.test.js`, fixtures fork named JS files and tools rely on resource-relative paths.
Use explicit compilation into an isolated test execution tree where appropriate;
copy/resolve resources and subprocess entries deliberately. Existing command names
must discover and execute the same behavioral suites. Do not raise the Node
minimum or introduce a global TS loader/`NODE_OPTIONS` preload.

Build tools must bootstrap from checked-in executable outputs or a tiny explicitly
checked compiler launcher, never from unavailable unbuilt TS. Keep config loaders
compatible; small JS config/bootstrap exceptions need strict `checkJs` and a
named rationale where the host requires them. Intentional syntax/loader fixtures
remain distinct test data, not unchecked application implementations.

**Acceptance:** actual test/tool bodies checked; no blanket `test/`/`scripts/`
exception, loss of discovery or weakened assertions; clean `npm ci` followed by
documented commands works. Test conversion is not permission for wholesale test
restructuring. R12 can then replace the migrated vendor loader.

### C2 — Enforced source inventory and final delivery audit

**Depends on:** M, R and C1 completion; basic accounting can be introduced in M0.

Every tracked repository-owned executable JS/MJS/CJS/TS path must belong to one
compiler-owned implementation, generated-output mapping, or named justified
exception. Reject unclassified additions, missing/stale/orphan outputs and stale
exceptions. Enumerate deliberate fixture/vendor/historical-doc data separately.
Shell installers/tmux/tailnet scripts remain shell with behavior coverage;
preserve lock-FD inheritance and exit-code contracts. Do not touch the ignored
machine-local `launch-tailnet.sh` or credentials.

Mark only genuine generated outputs for GitHub Linguist; never hide all `lib/*.js`
or tests to manufacture a TS percentage. Retain the independent browser/helper
entrypoints: VM/parity/fixture/ESLint consumers still use them. Their removal would
require a separate consumer cutover, not an accounting change.

**Final completion gate:** no unclassified first-party implementation; all native
entrypoints and supported package paths exercised; all R deletion ledgers met;
temporary scaffolding removed; docs/build commands/coverage map reflect reality;
full required suites and exact pushed-commit CI green. Publish source coverage,
compiler coverage, simplification results and delivery evidence separately.
Product migration is not declared repository completion until this gate passes.

## Dependency waves and integration ownership

1. **Freeze:** M0 delivery/inventory and the small shared M1 projection/SDK and
   M3/M5 artifact/transport contracts. This establishes worker interfaces, not
   speculative implementations.
2. **Parallel migration:** M1a/b/c with explicit SDK/index editors; M2 store/
   provenance/cron; M3 stores/files; M5 transport/PTY; M6 extension/CLI/Electron
   checking. M4 independent agent/STT work can start here.
3. **Integrate migration:** M2 prompts wait for refs; M4 aggregation waits for
   M1; M3 export/remote integration waits for M1/M5; M7 serializes server-family
   integration and closes the complete product inventory. M6 runtime proofs finish.
4. **Parallel refactors after the product gate:** R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7,
   R8, R10 and R11 can own separate files where contracts are stable. Serialize
   shared index, server and bridge edits; R1/R4 also serialize their shared mining
   primitive cutover. R9 follows R8. Do not run validation against another
   worker's half-integrated tree.
5. **Repository closure:** C1 loader mapping precedes test-family conversion;

Use one integration owner for `server` composition, one for `session-index`, one
for Pi SDK/extension adapter signatures and one for browser `app.ts`/selection
ports. A worker owns source plus its callers and evidence, not an isolated
declaration. Independent work can be implemented in parallel; overlapping file
edits and producer/consumer contract changes are serialized explicitly.

## Planning evidence and critique gate

Four read-only workers ran as **`openai-codex/gpt-6-astra`**, high reasoning, with

…

The naive comparison is dominated by an expected, systematic artifact: **esbuild converts single-quoted string literals to double-quoted ones** (its printer prefers `"`), and it re-joins multi-line string concatenations. That's why nearly every diff is the same literal with `'` vs `"` quotes — e.g. `'"map is read-only"'` vs `"\"map is read-only\""`, `'xml'` vs `"xml"`. Also:
- Producer multi-line concatenated keyword strings (split across lines with `+`) appear as separate producer literals vs one joined bundle literal (e.g. lua/r/kotlin built_in lists) — esbuild kept the concatenation expression, but my regex matched each segment separately on the producer side; on the bundle side the segments are on ONE line so my `[^'\\\n]` pattern... wait, bundle side shows them as one literal because esbuild joined the string *literals* — no, esbuild didn't fold; the bundle literal in output is `"abs" "accept"...` — look at perl: bundle-only `"abs" "accept"...` are individual double-quoted, producer-only `'abs' 'accept'...` individual single-quoted — that's just quote-style. For lua/r the producer has multi-line string *concatenation* where each line-fragment is a separate literal like `'_G _ENV _VERSION __index __newindex __mode __call __metatable __tostring __len '` (with trailing space), while bundle shows one long joined literal — meaning esbuild DID fold adjacent string concatenation (it does fold `+` of string literals even without minify — yes, esbuild's printer merges adjacent string literal concatenations). The joined bundle literal equals the concatenation of producer fragments (visible in lua/r cases — content matches).
- `"node_modules/highlight.js/lib/X.js"` bundle-only: that's the esbuild `__commonJS` module key property — generated by esbuild, expected.
- COUNT-DIFFs: quote style again (producer `'x'` count vs bundle `"x"` count — my filter `!p.has(k)` on exact string including quotes; count-diff arises when the same double-quoted literal exists in producer but with different multiplicity after folding).

So the check as written can't distinguish quote-style. Fix: normalize by stripping the outer quote and comparing content multisets. That directly tests content equality of string literals modulo esbuild's known quote preference and concatenation folding. For concatenation folding, joined bundle literal ≠ any single producer literal — content multiset will differ (one long string vs several fragments). To handle: additionally verify each bundle-only content is a concatenation of consecutive producer-only fragments... getting complicated. 

Simpler robust approach: compare the **sorted set of all string-literal CONTENT** per module after also generating the "folded" producer view: compute producer content multiset, then also merge — no.

Better: use my earlier verified stronger signals — the runtime parity probe (behavioral equality, 36 languages, byte-identical outputs) plus this content check with quote normalization, treating only these acceptable residue classes:
1. esbuild module key literal (path).
2. Producer fragments whose concatenation appears joined in bundle (adjacent `+` concatenations) — verify by checking the joined bundle-only content equals concatenation of some producer-only contents in order.
3. Producer `./core`/`./languages/x` require specifiers (common.js — esbuild replaced requires with function calls).

Implement: normalize content (strip quotes), build multisets; for each bundle-only content not in producer contents, check (a) it's the module path key, or (b) it can be formed by concatenating producer-only contents — greedy match in producer order. If all bundle-only items fall into (a)/(b) and no producer-only content remains unexplained modulo (b)-consumption and comment text, then parity holds. The comment-explanation check from v1 was too strict because of quote-style too — redo with content matching inside comment text.

Let me rewrite the probe accordingly.

content.text:
---
name: pi-dish-sessions
description: Spawn, message, and read ordinary peer Pi sessions through the pi-dish server, and search every past session transcript — locally or across the whole host fleet. Use when work should run in a separate durable Pi process, when another session needs a prompt, steer, follow-up, interrupt, resume, or graceful termination, when a prompt carries a session ref or a `#ref` mention (like "#tycho/8f3ab2c1") or a `<session-refs>` block and you need to read or talk to that session, or when prior sessions may already hold the answer (how something was fixed or built before, where a file was touched, what a past investigation concluded).
---

# Pi-dish peer sessions

Use the bundled CLI. It talks only to pi-dish's semantic HTTP routes; it
never writes Pi JSONL or signals processes itself.

```bash
CLI=~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-dish-sessions/scripts/pi-dish-sessions.js
node "$CLI" list --active
```

`PI_DISH_URL` is inherited by sessions spawned through pi-dish and otherwise
defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:3333`; set `PI_DISH_TOKEN` when the server
requires a bearer. The CLI identifies the current session automatically; use
`--session <id>` only if it reports ambiguity. `--json` everywhere for
machine-readable output.

## Session refs

Anywhere a command takes a session id, it takes a **ref**: a full id, its
uuid tail, a unique ≥4-char prefix of either (`01a070d2`), or a
host-qualified form (`tycho/01a070d2` — no `--host` needed). `list`,
`search` and `resolve` print the shortest ref for each session in their
first column; pass that along. Never retype an encoded `~sk1_…` route id —
it is ~100 base64 characters and a one-character slip still decodes, so the
server can only say `Session not found`. Users copy refs from the pi-dish
UI; treat a pasted short id as a ref, and `resolve <ref>` to see what it
points at.

A prompt written in the pi-dish composer can carry `#ref` mentions, and the
server appends a `<session-refs>` block listing each one with its name, host
and cwd. Those are live handles, not citations: `read` the session before
reasoning about what it did, and `send`/`steer`/`follow-up` to talk to it.

## Hot path

```bash
node "$CLI" search "jsonl torn tail recovery" --limit 5   # find prior work
node "$CLI" search "index compaction" --all-hosts          # whole fleet
node "$CLI" read tycho/8f3ab2c1                            # transcript as markdown
node "$CLI" send <ref> "Run the tests"                     # prompt (queues mid-turn)
node "$CLI" steer <ref> "Check the nested case first"      # redirect current turn
node "$CLI" follow-up <ref> "Then summarize here"          # queue for after the turn
node "$CLI" spawn --cwd "$PWD" --name "investigation" \
  --prompt "Investigate the cache issue and report" --json # durable peer process
node "$CLI" resume <ref>                                   # revive an inactive session
```

A spawned peer runs the same harness as the session spawning it (Pi from Pi,
OMP from OMP), so it has the same tools and skills you do. Pass
`--harness pi|omp|prime` to cross over deliberately; the spawn result names
the harness it launched.

displayContent.text:
---
name: pi-dish-sessions
description: Spawn, message, and read ordinary peer Pi sessions through the pi-dish server, and search every past session transcript — locally or across the whole host fleet. Use when work should run in a separate durable Pi process, when another session needs a prompt, steer, follow-up, interrupt, resume, or graceful termination, when a prompt carries a session ref or a `#ref` mention (like "#tycho/8f3ab2c1") or a `<session-refs>` block and you need to read or talk to that session, or when prior sessions may already hold the answer (how something was fixed or built before, where a file was touched, what a past investigation concluded).
---

# Pi-dish peer sessions

Use the bundled CLI. It talks only to pi-dish's semantic HTTP routes; it
never writes Pi JSONL or signals processes itself.

```bash
CLI=~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-dish-sessions/scripts/pi-dish-sessions.js
node "$CLI" list --active
```

`PI_DISH_URL` is inherited by sessions spawned through pi-dish and otherwise
defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:3333`; set `PI_DISH_TOKEN` when the server
requires a bearer. The CLI identifies the current session automatically; use
`--session <id>` only if it reports ambiguity. `--json` everywhere for
machine-readable output.

## Session refs

Anywhere a command takes a session id, it takes a **ref**: a full id, its
uuid tail, a unique ≥4-char prefix of either (`01a070d2`), or a
host-qualified form (`tycho/01a070d2` — no `--host` needed). `list`,
`search` and `resolve` print the shortest ref for each session in their
first column; pass that along. Never retype an encoded `~sk1_…` route id —
it is ~100 base64 characters and a one-character slip still decodes, so the
server can only say `Session not found`. Users copy refs from the pi-dish
UI; treat a pasted short id as a ref, and `resolve <ref>` to see what it
points at.

A prompt written in the pi-dish composer can carry `#ref` mentions, and the
server appends a `<session-refs>` block listing each one with its name, host
and cwd. Those are live handles, not citations: `read` the session before
reasoning about what it did, and `send`/`steer`/`follow-up` to talk to it.

## Hot path

```bash
node "$CLI" search "jsonl torn tail recovery" --limit 5   # find prior work
node "$CLI" search "index compaction" --all-hosts          # whole fleet
node "$CLI" read tycho/8f3ab2c1                            # transcript as markdown
node "$CLI" send <ref> "Run the tests"                     # prompt (queues mid-turn)
node "$CLI" steer <ref> "Check the nested case first"      # redirect current turn
node "$CLI" follow-up <ref> "Then summarize here"          # queue for after the turn
node "$CLI" spawn --cwd "$PWD" --name "investigation" \
  --prompt "Investigate the cache issue and report" --json # durable peer process
node "$CLI" resume <ref>                                   # revive an inactive session
```

A spawned peer runs the same harness as the session spawning it (Pi from Pi,
OMP from OMP), so it has the same tools and skills you do. Pass
`--harness pi|omp|prime` to cross over deliberately; the spawn result names
the harness it launched.

Search treats the session corpus as long-term memory: before re-deriving a
fix, config, or investigation, check whether a prior session already did it.
If a first query misses, reformulate with terms you'd expect *in the
transcript* — an error string, a file path, a command line. Search finds the
session; `read` reads it.

Also available: `show` (raw JSON window), `related`, `interrupt`, `close`
(graceful, no force-kill), `hosts` (the fleet; `--host <name>` puts any
command on that host), `attach` (join a live session's tmux pane from this
terminal — local only), `resolve`, `session`.

## Going deeper

- `node "$CLI" --help` and `help <command>` — full flags and examples.
- `node "$CLI" docs` — server-versioned topics (`refs`, `search` grammar,
  `fleet` semantics, `sessions` control details). In a mixed-version fleet
  the server's own docs beat this file; `docs --host <name>` reads a peer's.

…

…
**Proof:** no per-mutation factory allocation or host-argument substitution;
…
and patching the original session after selection changes. Existing API/control/
delayed-mutation/endpoint-change cases plus real multi-host UI smoke are gates.

### R11 — One canonical reference algorithm across app and skill client

**After:** M6b. Bundle existing portable `src/core/helper-refs.ts` behavior into
the generated skill client; remove its copies of alias generation, staged
resolution and stable/short references. Keep the installed client dependency-free.

**Proof:** one authored algorithm; existing semantic precedence/ambiguity/
host-qualified exact-only cases pass through real CLI and browser/server paths.
Preserve the CLI's differing missing-native-ID parsing policy explicitly; do not
blindly replace its decoder with stricter canonical decoding. Remove copy-parity
tests that become wiring assertions, retaining consumer behavior coverage.

### R12 — Remove the handwritten vendor module loader

**After:** the vendor-tool source/runner portion of C1 is ready (it may land
earlier than the remainder of C1). Use existing pinned esbuild for the local
highlight bundle instead of `build-vendor`'s dependency collector and generated
`__mods`/`__cache`/`__req` implementation.

**Proof:** manual loader/resolver/cache wrappers deleted; `window.hljs`, common
languages, licenses and offline highlighting preserved. CSS/fonts and unrelated
vendor delivery stay unchanged. Rebuild vendor outputs only for this package;
exercise actual offline code rendering. No new bundler abstraction.

### Deliberate limits on refactoring

The scoping workers identified possible stale-stat/short-read index publication
risks, but did not reproduce corruption. M1's malformed/append/truncate matrix
must exercise the consumed-byte/stamp invariant. A demonstrated violation becomes
a focused regression/fix; a speculative transactional index/cache rewrite is not
part of the mandatory refactor list. No stronger atomicity claim is made here.

Also excluded: unifying differing header/cwd/recovery parsers; a generic terminal
routine “finish and close”; merging pricing persistence with generic store writes
despite permission/newline differences; merging interactive/pricing command
runners; broad host-catalog extraction from new-session forms; framework adoption.
Future ideas require their own problem/evidence, not expansion of this finish line.

## Phase C — Repository closure

### C1 — Checked tests, fixtures, development tools and configurations

**Depends on:** stable product contracts. Its runner/vendor-tool prerequisite may
start alongside late M/R work; test-family cutovers wait for the contract they use.

Convert the authored scripts (nine at baseline, plus M0's source-policy gate and
later additions), Node tests, Playwright tests, UI scenarios and support
implementations in bounded families. Explicitly allocate
`eslint.config.js` and `playwright.config.js`: keep compatible loader entrypoints
as named strict-`checkJs` configurations unless their hosts support a direct TS
cutover without a new runtime loader. Their bodies are checked, not deferred to
the final audit. Keep Node and browser-evaluation compiler environments separate.
Preserve intentional malformed inputs as unknown or explicit negative cases
rather than weakening product types.

Freeze the execution mapping before renaming: `run-tests.js` discovers only
`.test.js`, fixtures fork named JS files and tools rely on resource-relative paths.
Use explicit compilation into an isolated test execution tree where appropriate;
copy/resolve resources and subprocess entries deliberately. Existing command names
must discover and execute the same behavioral suites. Do not raise the Node
minimum or introduce a global TS loader/`NODE_OPTIONS` preload.

Build tools must bootstrap from checked-in executable outputs or a tiny explicitly
checked compiler launcher, never from unavailable unbuilt TS. Keep config loaders
compatible; small JS config/bootstrap exceptions need strict `checkJs` and a
named rationale where the host requires them. Intentional syntax/loader fixtures
remain distinct test data, not unchecked application implementations.

**Acceptance:** actual test/tool bodies checked; no blanket `test/`/`scripts/`
exception, loss of discovery or weakened assertions; clean `npm ci` followed by
documented commands works. Test conversion is not permission for wholesale test
restructuring. R12 can then replace the migrated vendor loader.

### C2 — Enforced source inventory and final delivery audit

**Depends on:** M, R and C1 completion; basic accounting can be introduced in M0.

Every tracked repository-owned executable JS/MJS/CJS/TS path must belong to one
compiler-owned implementation, generated-output mapping, or named justified
exception. Reject unclassified additions, missing/stale/orphan outputs and stale
exceptions. Enumerate deliberate fixture/vendor/historical-doc data separately.
Shell installers/tmux/tailnet scripts remain shell with behavior coverage;
preserve lock-FD inheritance and exit-code contracts. Do not touch the ignored
machine-local `launch-tailnet.sh` or credentials.

Mark only genuine generated outputs for GitHub Linguist; never hide all `lib/*.js`
or tests to manufacture a TS percentage. Retain the independent browser/helper
entrypoints: VM/parity/fixture/ESLint consumers still use them. Their removal would
require a separate consumer cutover, not an accounting change.

**Final completion gate:** no unclassified first-party implementation; all native
entrypoints and supported package paths exercised; all R deletion ledgers met;
temporary scaffolding removed; docs/build commands/coverage map reflect reality;
full required suites and exact pushed-commit CI green. Publish source coverage,
compiler coverage, simplification results and delivery evidence separately.
Product migration is not declared repository completion until this gate passes.

   speculative implementations.

   provenance/cron; M3 stores/files; M5 transport/PTY; M6 extension/CLI/Electron
   checking. M4 independent agent/STT work can start here.

   M1; M3 export/remote integration waits for M1/M5; M7 serializes server-family
   integration and closes the complete product inventory. M6 runtime proofs finish.

   worker's half-integrated tree.
5. **Repository closure:** C1 loader mapping precedes test-family conversion;
   its vendor-tool slice unlocks R12. C2 audits the final result.

for Pi SDK/extension adapter signatures and one for browser `app.ts`/selection
ports. A worker owns source plus its callers and evidence, not an isolated
declaration. Independent work can be implemented in parallel; overlapping file
edits and producer/consumer contract changes are serialized explicitly.

Four read-only workers ran as **`openai-codex/gpt-6-astra`**, high reasoning, with

runtime/compiler closure. Their returned provider/model identities were checked.
They did not run implementation tests or change repository files.

`ready`**, with no unresolved original findings or blocking/important new findings.
The rechecks added three minor clarifications: same-object SSE replay state,
M0-versus-M7 launcher timing, and mood's real TUI/TypeBox declaration sources.
Those are incorporated above, with source-premise corrections recorded explicitly.

The [complete critique and resolution record](remaining-migration-review-2026-09-15.json)
retains the initial verdicts, exact reviewed digests, actual provider/model/session
identities, rechecks and maintainer dispositions. Rechecked scope is distinguished
from these final minor clarifications and review-status/link changes; it is not
represented as a third independent review of the final bytes.

import re, glob, os
bundle = open('public/vendor/highlight.js', encoding='utf-8').read()
blines = bundle.split('\n')
# upstream union
up = set()
files = ['node_modules/highlight.js/lib/core.js','node_modules/highlight.js/lib/common.js'] + sorted(glob.glob('node_modules/highlight.js/lib/languages/*.js'))
upfiles = {}
for f in files:
    src = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read()
    upfiles[f] = src
    for l in src.split('\n'):
        up.add(l.strip())
def norm(l):
    l = l.strip()
    l = re.sub(r'\$(\d+)', '', l)          # esbuild rename suffix
    l = l.replace('_TokenTree.', 'TokenTree.')
    return l
upn = {norm(l) for l in up}
wrapper = []
unexplained = []
for i, l in enumerate(blines, 1):
    s = l.strip()
    if s == '': continue
    if s in up or norm(l) in upn: continue
    if (s.startswith('// node_modules/') or s.startswith('var require_')
        or s.startswith('__commonJS') or s.startswith('var __getOwnPropNames')
        or s.startswith('var __commonJS') or s in ('(() => {', '})();', ')();')
        or s.startswith('"node_modules/highlight.js/')
        or s.startswith('window.hljs = require_common()')
        or s.startswith('return mod || (0, cb[') or s.startswith('throw mod = 0, e;')
        or s.startswith('return mod ||') or s.startswith('try {') or s.startswith('} catch (e)')
        or s == 'try {' or s.startswith('/* highlight.js common bundle')):
        wrapper.append((i, s)); continue
    unexplained.append((i, s))
print('bundle lines:', len(blines))
print('wrapper/known lines:', len(wrapper))
print('unexplained lines:', len(unexplained))
for i, s in unexplained[:60]:
    print('  ', i, s[:160])
# module inventory
mods = re.findall(r'// (node_modules/highlight\.js/[^\n]+)', bundle)
print('module headers:', len(mods), 'unique:', len(set(mods)))
langs = [m for m in mods if '/languages/' in m]
print('language modules:', len(langs))
print('expected language files:', len(glob.glob('node_modules/highlight.js/lib/languages/*.js')))
extra = set(mods) - set(files)
missing = set(files) - set(mods)
print('module headers not in upstream list:', extra)
print('upstream files not bundled:', sorted(missing))

content.text:
## Messaging a session

Three delivery semantics, all queue-safe:

- `send <ref> "..."` — a normal prompt. If the target is mid-turn, pi queues
  it; otherwise it starts a turn.
- `steer <ref> "..."` — delivered *into* the current turn, redirecting work
  in progress. Use when the target is actively working and should change
  course now.
- `follow-up <ref> "..."` — queued for after the current turn completes.
  Use for "then also do X" while a turn runs.

A queued message can be seen and cancelled by the user in the pi-dish UI, and
by the target's own TUI. There is no inbox: a message to an inactive session
means `resume <ref>` first, then `follow-up`.

## Reading a session (memory recall)

`read <ref>` renders the transcript as markdown: turn headers, prose in
--

- `spawn --cwd DIR [--name N] [--harness ID] [--model provider/id]
  [--prompt "..."]` — spawns an ordinary, durable agent process (not a
  subagent). The harness defaults to the one the calling session runs on, so
  an OMP session spawns OMP and a Pi session spawns Pi; `--harness` crosses
  over, and the target host is checked for that harness before launching.
  `--no-wait` returns the spawn id immediately. Launch provenance is recorded
  in an advisory sidecar so the UI can navigate between related sessions; it
  grants no ownership or lifecycle authority.
--
### Bulk maintenance

Settings → **Bounce agents** queues a snapshot of owned runtimes. Each host
advertises `capabilities.sessionBounces`; clients aggregate capable hosts,
not the server.

- `GET /api/session-bounces/preview?mode=reload|restart` returns active
  targets with eligibility, reasons, and current safety blockers.
- `POST /api/session-bounces` with `{mode, sessionIds}` returns
  `202 {operation}`. Only explicit IDs are considered; unknown/unowned or
  already-queued targets are skipped.
- `GET /api/session-bounces` returns `{operations}` with per-target
  `waiting`, `executing`, `completed`, `skipped`, `failed`, or `cancelled`
  status and a reason. Successful restarts include `replacementId`.
- `DELETE /api/session-bounces/:id` cancels waiting targets only.

Use Reload for Pi extension changes; use Restart for runtime upgrades or
--
there is no typed-command fallback and no implicit switch to Restart.

Working/compacting parents, queued messages, open input dialogs, and OMP
background jobs or pending deliveries block execution. **Every OMP child
must exit, including idle kept-alive children.** Unknown safety state or
incomplete descendant discovery also blocks. Old bridges lacking safety
reporting require a manual upgrade/restart first.

Runtime identity and safety are rechecked before execution, using the
--
TUI input: do not start a new turn there while maintenance is executing.
The individual Restart agent control remains an immediate manual action;

---
name: pi-dish-sessions
description: Spawn, message, and read ordinary peer Pi sessions through the pi-dish server, and search every past session transcript — locally or across the whole host fleet. Use when work should run in a separate durable Pi process, when another session needs a prompt, steer, follow-up, interrupt, resume, or graceful termination, when a prompt carries a session ref or a `#ref` mention (like "#tycho/8f3ab2c1") or a `<session-refs>` block and you need to read or talk to that session, or when prior sessions may already hold the answer (how something was fixed or built before, where a file was touched, what a past investigation concluded).
---

# Pi-dish peer sessions

Use the bundled CLI. It talks only to pi-dish's semantic HTTP routes; it
never writes Pi JSONL or signals processes itself.

```bash
CLI=~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-dish-sessions/scripts/pi-dish-sessions.js
node "$CLI" list --active
```

`PI_DISH_URL` is inherited by sessions spawned through pi-dish and otherwise
defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:3333`; set `PI_DISH_TOKEN` when the server
requires a bearer. The CLI identifies the current session automatically; use
`--session <id>` only if it reports ambiguity. `--json` everywhere for
machine-readable output.

## Session refs

Anywhere a command takes a session id, it takes a **ref**: a full id, its
uuid tail, a unique ≥4-char prefix of either (`01a070d2`), or a
host-qualified form (`tycho/01a070d2` — no `--host` needed). `list`,
`search` and `resolve` print the shortest ref for each session in their
first column; pass that along. Never retype an encoded `~sk1_…` route id —
it is ~100 base64 characters and a one-character slip still decodes, so the
server can only say `Session not found`. Users copy refs from the pi-dish
UI; treat a pasted short id as a ref, and `resolve <ref>` to see what it
points at.

A prompt written in the pi-dish composer can carry `#ref` mentions, and the
server appends a `<session-refs>` block listing each one with its name, host
and cwd. Those are live handles, not citations: `read` the session before
reasoning about what it did, and `send`/`steer`/`follow-up` to talk to it.

## Hot path

```bash
node "$CLI" search "jsonl torn tail recovery" --limit 5   # find prior work
node "$CLI" search "index compaction" --all-hosts          # whole fleet
node "$CLI" read tycho/8f3ab2c1                            # transcript as markdown
node "$CLI" send <ref> "Run the tests"                     # prompt (queues mid-turn)
node "$CLI" steer <ref> "Check the nested case first"      # redirect current turn
node "$CLI" follow-up <ref> "Then summarize here"          # queue for after the turn
node "$CLI" spawn --cwd "$PWD" --name "investigation" \
  --prompt "Investigate the cache issue and report" --json # durable peer process
node "$CLI" resume <ref>                                   # revive an inactive session
```

A spawned peer runs the same harness as the session spawning it (Pi from Pi,
OMP from OMP), so it has the same tools and skills you do. Pass
`--harness pi|omp|prime` to cross over deliberately; the spawn result names
the harness it launched.

Search treats the session corpus as long-term memory: before re-deriving a
fix, config, or investigation, check whether a prior session already did it.
If a first query misses, reformulate with terms you'd expect *in the
transcript* — an error string, a file path, a command line. Search finds the
session; `read` reads it.

Also available: `show` (raw JSON window), `related`, `interrupt`, `close`
(graceful, no force-kill), `hosts` (the fleet; `--host <name>` puts any
command on that host), `attach` (join a live session's tmux pane from this
terminal — local only), `resolve`, `session`.

## Going deeper

- `node "$CLI" --help` and `help <command>` — full flags and examples.
- `node "$CLI" docs` — server-versioned topics (`refs`, `search` grammar,
  `fleet` semantics, `sessions` control details). In a mixed-version fleet
  the server's own docs beat this file; `docs --host <name>` reads a peer's.

1:#!/usr/bin/env node
2:/**
3: * Builds public/vendor/ from node_modules so the frontend has zero CDN
4: * dependencies (phones on the LAN may not have internet; a missing CDN
5: * script used to silently disable markdown rendering).
6: *
7: *   node scripts/build-vendor.js
8: *
9: * Outputs:
10: *   public/vendor/marked.min.js      — copied from the marked package
11: *   public/vendor/highlight.js      — highlight.js common-languages bundle,
12: *                                      built with esbuild
13: *                                      (the npm package ships no browser build)
14: *   public/vendor/hljs-theme.min.css — highlight.js theme (solarized dark,
15: *                                      matching the app palette)
16: *   public/vendor/fonts/*.woff2     — modern KaTeX fonts only
17: *   public/vendor/xterm.js           — @xterm/xterm UMD build (browser terminal)
18: *   public/vendor/xterm.css          — its stylesheet
19: *   public/vendor/xterm-addon-fit.js — @xterm/addon-fit UMD build
20: *   public/vendor/mermaid.min.js     — mermaid IIFE build (diagram rendering,
21: *                                      loaded lazily on the first diagram)
22: */
23:import fs = require('fs');
24:import path = require('path');
25:import esbuild = require('esbuild');
26:
27:const root = path.join(__dirname, '..');
28:const outDir = path.join(root, 'public', 'vendor');
29:fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
30:
31:// --- marked: ships a browser UMD build, just copy it ---
32:fs.copyFileSync(
33:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', 'marked', 'marked.min.js'),
34:  path.join(outDir, 'marked.min.js'),
35:);
36:
37:// --- katex: copy browser bundle, css, and fonts ---
38:fs.copyFileSync(
39:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', 'katex', 'dist', 'katex.min.js'),
40:  path.join(outDir, 'katex.min.js'),
41:);
42:const katexCss = fs.readFileSync(
43:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', 'katex', 'dist', 'katex.min.css'), 'utf8')
44:  .replace(/,url\(([^)]*\.woff)\) format\("woff"\),url\(([^)]*\.ttf)\) format\("truetype"\)/g, '');
45:fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'katex.min.css'), katexCss);
46:const fontsIn = path.join(root, 'node_modules', 'katex', 'dist', 'fonts');
47:const fontsOut = path.join(outDir, 'fonts');
48:// Remove fallback formats left by an older build; modern supported browsers
49:// use WOFF2, so packaging WOFF and TTF triples build size for no runtime gain.
50:fs.rmSync(fontsOut, { recursive: true, force: true });
51:fs.mkdirSync(fontsOut, { recursive: true });
52:for (const font of fs.readdirSync(fontsIn)) {
53:  if (font.endsWith('.woff2')) fs.copyFileSync(path.join(fontsIn, font), path.join(fontsOut, font));
54:}
55:
56:// --- mermaid: dist/mermaid.min.js is a self-contained IIFE that assigns
57:// globalThis.mermaid (the .esm build splits into chunks that a plain <script>
58:// can't resolve). 3.5MB, so app.js loads it lazily on the first diagram. ---
59:fs.copyFileSync(
60:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', 'mermaid', 'dist', 'mermaid.min.js'),
61:  path.join(outDir, 'mermaid.min.js'),
62:);
63:
64:// --- xterm.js: ships browser UMD builds, just copy them ---
65:fs.copyFileSync(
66:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', '@xterm', 'xterm', 'lib', 'xterm.js'),
67:  path.join(outDir, 'xterm.js'),
68:);
69:fs.copyFileSync(
70:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', '@xterm', 'xterm', 'css', 'xterm.css'),
71:  path.join(outDir, 'xterm.css'),
72:);
73:fs.copyFileSync(
74:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', '@xterm', 'addon-fit', 'lib', 'addon-fit.js'),
75:  path.join(outDir, 'xterm-addon-fit.js'),
76:);
77:
78:// --- highlight.js theme css ---
79:fs.copyFileSync(
80:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', 'highlight.js', 'styles', 'base16', 'solarized-dark.min.css'),
81:  path.join(outDir, 'hljs-theme.min.css'),
82:);
83:
84:// --- highlight.js: bundle the common languages as one local browser script ---
85:const hljsPkg: Record<string, unknown> = require(path.join(root, 'node_modules', 'highlight.js', 'package.json'));
86:const hljsLicense = fs.readFileSync(
87:  path.join(root, 'node_modules', 'highlight.js', 'LICENSE'), 'utf-8').trim();
88:esbuild.buildSync({
89:  absWorkingDir: root,
90:  stdin: { contents: "window.hljs = require('highlight.js/lib/common');", resolveDir: root },
91:  bundle: true,
92:  platform: 'browser',
93:  format: 'iife',
94:  target: 'es2022',
95:  outfile: path.join(outDir, 'highlight.js'),
96:  banner: { js: `/* highlight.js common bundle — generated by scripts/build-vendor.js */\n/*!\nhighlight.js v${hljsPkg.version}\nhttps://github.com/highlightjs/highlight.js\n\n${hljsLicense}\n*/` },
97:});
98:console.log('vendor bundle written: hljs common languages, marked, katex (woff2), xterm, mermaid, hljs theme css');
